cases.question: In exactly two sentences, explain why wall-clock adjustments can break elapsed-time measurements and name a suitable alternative clock.
cases.reference: Wall clocks can move forward/backward under corrections, producing incorrect elapsed durations. A monotonic clock is appropriate for elapsed intervals; it does not provide a universal calendar timestamp.

criteria.task: In exactly two sentences, explain the adjustment problem and name a suitable alternative clock.
criteria.grounding: Do not assert that wall-clock differences are immune to clock corrections or that monotonic values are universal calendar timestamps.

cases.question: Give exactly three bullet points: one benefit of bulkheads, one benefit of a circuit breaker, and one limitation shared by both.
cases.reference: Bulkheads isolate resources/failure impact; circuit breakers avoid repeatedly calling a failing dependency; neither by itself repairs the dependency or guarantees successful requests. Three bullets, one requested item each.

criteria.task: Use exactly three bullets covering the two named benefits and one shared limitation.
criteria.grounding: Do not claim either pattern guarantees success or repairs an unavailable dependency.
criteria.clarification: Answer the three requested items directly.

cases.question: In exactly two sentences, distinguish a cache miss from cache invalidation and give one cause of each.
cases.reference: A miss is a requested item being absent/unavailable in the cache, for example on first access or after eviction. Invalidation marks/removes a cached value as unusable, for example after a source update or expiry; invalidation can cause a later miss.

criteria.task: In exactly two sentences, distinguish the two concepts and provide one cause of each.
criteria.grounding: Do not claim misses and invalidation are identical or mutually exclusive events.
criteria.clarification: Answer both specified concepts and causes directly.

cases.question: Give exactly two analogies for pacing outgoing requests, one sentence per analogy.
cases.reference: Two apt analogies for regulating request rate/timing, such as a metronome or timed release through a gate. Exactly two sentences, one analogy each; pacing does not guarantee remote success.

criteria.task: Give exactly two apt pacing analogies in exactly two sentences, one per analogy.
criteria.grounding: Do not make false claims about request rate, concurrency or guaranteed downstream success.

cases.question: In exactly two sentences, explain why retrying at several service layers can multiply total attempts and name one way to limit that amplification.
cases.reference: Each upstream retry can trigger a fresh set of downstream retries, multiplying attempts across layers. A shared retry budget, a single designated retry layer or another concrete bound can limit amplification.

criteria.task: In exactly two sentences, explain the multiplicative effect and name one concrete mitigation.
criteria.grounding: Do not assert that independent retry loops automatically coordinate or guarantee bounded total attempts without a bound.
